deep.reconstruction:
Context (my identification): this is an editorial insertion sheet ('Seite 32 unten' = to be inserted at the bottom of p. 32, sheet no. 2). It belongs to the material behind Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', prepared by Hattendorff and published in the Göttinger Abhandlungen 13 (1867). It concerns minimal surfaces bounded by straight-line segments. The handwriting may be Hattendorff's rather than Riemann's.

Setting, partly reconstructed by me. The surface is described through its Gauss map: eta is the stereographic coordinate of the unit normal. An auxiliary uniformizing variable t has its real axis corresponding to the boundary, and v is a further auxiliary variable. A function k satisfies a second-order linear ODE, equation (15), of the form d^2k/dv^2 = Q(v) k. Its solutions are built from eta and dt.

For each straight boundary segment, the spherical image is an arc of a great circle. One rotates the sphere by a rotation, i.e. a unitary Moebius transformation eta -> eta_1, so that this great circle becomes the equator |eta_1| = 1. Let k_1' be the corresponding function built from eta_1.

Step 1. The first line of the page reads '... der Differentialgleichung (15) sind'. So k and k_1' both satisfy (15), with the same coefficient. Hence
  (1/k) d^2k/dv^2 = (1/k_1') d^2k_1'/dv^2  ( = Q ).

Step 2. On this boundary piece eta_1 = e^{i phi_1}. Substituting this into k_1', one 'easily sees' that (1/k_1') k_1''(v) is real there. Implicitly dv is real or purely imaginary along the boundary.

Step 3. Therefore Q = k''/k is real on that piece. The argument applies to every boundary piece, so Q is real on the whole boundary. This is the reality condition that allows Q, and hence (15), to be continued by reflection and determined as a rational/algebraic expression with prescribed singularities, in the Riemann–Schwarz manner.

Step 4 (caveat). The reality of k_1''/k_1' for real or imaginary dv persists under the more general substitution eta_1 = rho_1 e^{i phi_1} with constant modulus rho_1. Under inverse stereographic projection, |eta_1| = rho_1 != 1 is a small circle (a parallel), not a great circle. So reality of Q alone does not force the spherical images of the boundary pieces to be great circles.

Step 5. For the real t-axis really to map onto arcs of great circles on the unit sphere, one must additionally impose rho_1 = 1 for every boundary piece. This gives exactly as many conditional equations as there are boundary lines. These are equations for the accessory constants of the problem.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The claim that (1/k_1') d^2k_1'/dv^2 is real on |eta_1| = const is asserted as 'leicht' without proof. It depends on the precise definition of k_1' and v (on the preceding pages, not available), so it cannot be fully verified here.
Step 3 implicitly uses that the rotation eta -> eta_1 leaves equation (15) invariant (k and k_1' solve the same ODE). This is stated as following from the previous page, which is missing.

results.what: Invariance of the coefficient (1/k)k'' of the linear ODE under rotation of the sphere (Moebius change eta -> eta_1); its reality on each straight boundary piece, hence on the whole boundary
results.modern_name: Schwarzian-derivative / linear-ODE method for the Plateau problem with polygonal boundary (Gauss map plus Weierstrass–Enneper data, reflection principle)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous memoir 1867, ed. Hattendorff); H. A. Schwarz (1865–1872); Weierstrass (1866)

results.what: Reality of k''/k is necessary but not sufficient: circles |eta_1| = rho_1 also give it; one must impose rho_1 = 1 for each boundary line (one condition per line) so that the images are great circles
results.modern_name: Determination of accessory parameters / period-type conditions for polygonal minimal surfaces
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's minimal-surface memoir; later Schwarz, Garnier (1928)

deep.surprise_reason: The content belongs to Riemann's minimal-surface memoir, published posthumously by Hattendorff in 1867. This sheet looks like an editorial or explanatory insertion ('Seite 32 unten') into that published text, so it is not new.

checkable.asserts: For a power-type function k = eta_1^a with eta_1 = rho*e^{iv}, k''/k = -a^2 is real independently of rho. This illustrates why reality alone does not force rho_1 = 1.
If k'' = Q k (here Q = c), the ratio w of two solutions has Schwarzian derivative -2Q. So Q is a Moebius-invariant of the map, consistent with k''/k = k_1''/k_1'. The expression should simplify to 0.
|eta| = 1 maps under inverse stereographic projection to the equator z = 0 (a great circle): the result is 1 with z = 0.

transcription_corrections: 'da zumal[?]' is doubtful. The image shows a short word pair before ', so ist' (possibly 'der Form' or similar); the reading is uncertain.
In 'Folglich gilt dasselbe von (1/k) d^2k/dy^2' the image has a sloppy 'dv^2' that looks like 'dy^2'. It should be dv^2.
The first line on the image is the fragment '...der Differentialgleichung (15) sind.' The opening of the sentence is on the previous sheet, so k and k_1' are 'solutions of' (15).
